I found no missing mathematical assumption, resource-sharing defect, or counterexample. The dedicated checker passed with assertions enabled, and both regenerated outputs agree with the supplied outputs structurally and byte-for-byte.The acceptance has the stated scope:  $U_1$  is the exact optimum within the specified normal form; it certifies the global optimum when it meets  $\Lambda$ . Under the two strict-positivity assumptions, it also decides whether the global optimum attains  $\Lambda$ . It is not being accepted as a general global optimizer when  $U_1>\Lambda$ .1. General criterion: the critical proof steps are validI reviewed the hypotheses and proofs in §§1–2 of    EXPOSABLE_PORTS_AND_BRANCHED_SOURCE_OBSTRUCTION.md, together with the source-budget definitions and the implementation.The maximum-discount augmentation preserves the property neededEvery black exterior vertex has a direct selected neighbour, witnessed by the black-saturating matching in  $G_O$ . Its shortest TH expense is therefore zero. The only potentially positive terminal benefits in the generic full- $Q$  source budget are the centre benefits  $\rho_i$ .The important assertion in the proof of equation (1) is correct:Augmenting a partial matching preserves the set of already matched right vertices and adds one new right vertex.It may change individual source-to-centre assignments. That does not affect the argument: the benefits depend only on which centres are matched. Since  $\rho_i\ge0$ , augmentation cannot decrease the total benefit.Because  $\Gamma$  has a matching saturating  $W$ , every partial matching can be augmented to size  $r-1$ . Such a matching omits exactly one centre  $j\in J$ , and its benefit is
$$\sum_{i=1}^{r}\rho_i-\rho_j.$$
Consequently the maximum discount is
$$\Delta=\sum_i\rho_i-\min_{j\in J}\rho_j,$$
which gives
$$\boxed{\Lambda=\min_{j\in J}\rho_j.}$$
Zero-benefit exterior assignments or zero-benefit centre assignments do not invalidate this calculation.The exposure lemma and the two matching choices fit togetherThe standard exposure lemma is correctly stated and proved. Two left-saturating matchings in a surplus-one bipartite graph have a symmetric-difference path joining their two exposed right vertices, unless those vertices coincide; the remaining nontrivial components are alternating cycles. This gives both the reachability characterization and the path-flip construction.For equation (2), choosing  $j\in J$  and a relay from  $t\in E$  to  $h_j$  is sufficient:A matching in  $\Gamma$  assigns each white hole to a different remaining centre.There is exactly one relay in each core.Different relay interiors lie in disjoint  $P_i$ , and all terminal endpoints are distinct.Every interior vertex on a relay is used together with its actual  $M$ -mate.Thus the selected auxiliary relay edges coexist. Doubling all unused  $M$ -edges covers the unused core vertices. The remaining uncovered set is exactly  $O\setminus\{t\}$ , which has a direct perfect matching because  $t\in E$ .Conversely, a full matching in the specified normal form supplies both an assignment witnessing  $j\in J$  and a direct exterior matching witnessing  $t\in E$ . Its paid expense is at least  $\sigma_j$ . Therefore
$$\boxed{U_1=\min_{j\in J}\sigma_j}$$
is precisely the normal-form optimum, including the possibility  $U_1=\infty$ .There is no assumption here that arbitrary independent routes through a shared core are compatible: the construction uses only one relay per core.The strict-positivity necessity proof is soundLet  $N$  attain  $\Lambda$ , and let  $S$  be its set of TH centres. Its actual HH-centre paths induce a partial matching in  $\Gamma$ .Augment that partial matching to a  $W$ -saturating matching. Because augmentation preserves every previously matched centre, its omitted centre  $j$  was originally TH. Hence  $j\in S\cap J$ , and disjointness of the physical terminal paths gives
$$f(N)\ge \sum_{i\in S}\rho_i\ge \rho_j\ge\Lambda.$$
If  $|S|\ge2$ , the assumption that every  $\rho_i>0$  makes the middle inequality strict. Equality therefore forces exactly one TH centre, whose path spends the entire budget.The other  $r-1$  centres are HH and consume all  $r-1$  white holes. Every remaining terminal path is consequently TH and has zero expense. Strict positivity of every actual weight then forces these paths to contain no actual edge; an alternating terminal path with no actual edge is direct.The resulting matching has the specified normal form, apart from irrelevant  $P$ -only components, which may be replaced by doubled  $M$ -edges. This proves
$$\boxed{f^*=\Lambda\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad U_1=\Lambda}$$
under exactly the two additional positivity assumptions.Zero weights and endpoint cases are correctly qualifiedThe positivity assumptions serve separate purposes:A zero  $\rho_i$  prevents the inference that two TH centres necessarily exceed the budget.A zero-weight actual edge prevents the inference that a zero-expense TH path must be direct.The note correctly retains sufficiency of  $U_1=\Lambda$  under nonnegative weights and does not assert necessity there.The case  $r=1$  also works:  $W=\varnothing$ ,  $J=\{1\}$ , and the construction consists of the single chosen TH relay and an exterior matching exposing its source. Direct centre relays are allowed by the definitions. Neither connectedness of  $\Gamma$  nor connectedness of the exterior is needed.2. The fixed 18-by-18 geometry and Hall certificate are validThe coordinates and matching lists in   branched_source_obstruction.py agree with the written construction.Independent coordinate checks confirmed: $324$  board vertices and  $120$  vertices in  $P$ ; $60$  actual matching edges and  $98$  selected white terminals;no grid adjacency between different  $P_i$ ;feasibility of every selected terminal;exactly the four stated white holes as the white  $Q$ -vertices having more than one  $P$ -neighbour.The source incidences are exactly:White HH sourceIncident cores $(5,10)$  $0,2$  $(6,5)$  $0,1$  $(10,11)$  $0,3$  $(11,6)$  $0,4$ Each incidence enters through a black corner. The corner-pad matching argument supplies an alternating source-to-centre relay for every internal rematching: compare an auxiliary matching of the square with its pad against the actual matching of the punctured square. Their tagged union contains the required alternating path. Separation prevents additional incidences through other cores.Thus the incidence graph is the asserted star, and every centre can be omitted:  $J=I$ .Exact exterior obstructionFor
$$D=([0,1]\times[0,9])\cup([2,5]\times[5,9]),$$
the independently reconstructed sets satisfy
$$|B_D|=|F|=20,

N_{G_O}(B_D)=F.$$
The only white  $Q$ -neighbours of  $B_D$  outside  $D$  are
$$(5,10),\qquad (6,5),$$
and both belong to  $W$ , so neither is available in  $G_O$ . The other board neighbours outside  $D$  belong to  $P$ .Deleting any  $t\in F$  therefore leaves these twenty exterior black vertices with only nineteen available white neighbours. In particular,
$$t_*=(5,8)\notin E.$$
The supplied exterior base matching covers all  $97$  black exterior vertices. The independent deletion checks also establish the stronger fixed-instance identity
$$E=T\setminus F,\qquad |E|=78.$$
These are exact coordinate and matching certificates; no extrapolation from a family of small examples is required.3. Both claimed physical optima are provedUnit rematching:  $f^*=U_1=2>\Lambda=1$ The four-neighbour inspection at each centre gives exactly
$$\bigl(\{(5,8)\},\varnothing,\varnothing,\varnothing,\varnothing\bigr)$$
for the possible selected sources of one-actual-edge centre relays. The supplied relay witnesses establish
$$\rho=(1,2,2,2,2).$$
Since  $J=I$ , the budget is  $\Lambda=1$ .With five black centres and four white HH sources, at least one centre must be TH. If  $f=1$ , that centre must be the central one and must use  $t_*$ . The four other centres consume all four HH sources. Every other TH path must then be direct, which would give a perfect matching of  $O\setminus\{t_*\}$ , contradicting the Hall certificate.Unit costs are integral, so this proves  $f\ge2$ .The supplied attaining matching uses the central TH path
$$(6,11),(6,10),(6,9),(6,8),(7,8),(8,8).$$
Its paid actual edges are exactly
$$\{(6,10),(6,9)\},
\qquad
\{(6,8),(7,8)\}.$$
The independent decomposition confirmed that the full auxiliary matching covers all  $324$  vertices with  $162$  edges, uses each white hole once, and has no shared actual resource. Its cost is two and it is in the specified normal form. Hence
$$\boxed{f^*=U_1=2>\Lambda=1.}$$
Canonical matching:  $f^*=U_1=K$  for every integer  $K\ge2$ The all- $K$  argument in §5 is valid independently of the six numerical controls.If  $f(N)<K$ , no TH path can use an actual edge other than
$$e_*=\{(6,8),(7,8)\}.$$
Some centre must be TH. It must therefore be the central centre, reached through  $e_*$ . The coordinates force both terminal incidences:
$$N((6,8))\cap T=\{(5,8)\},
\qquad
N((7,8))\cap Q=\{(8,8)\}.$$
Thus the cheap paid source is necessarily  $t_*$ .All four remaining centres must be HH and consume all four holes. Since the cheap edge is already owned by the central path, every remaining TH path must be direct. The same Hall contradiction proves  $f(N)\ge K$ .The supplied attaining matching instead uses
$$(8,5),(8,6),(8,7),(8,8).$$
Its only paid actual edge is
$$\{(8,6),(8,7)\},$$
which has weight  $K$ . The exterior matching exposes  $(8,5)$ , and the four HH sources have distinct arm assignments. This one physical matching attains  $K$  for every allowed  $K$ . Therefore
$$\boxed{\Lambda=1,\qquad f^*=U_1=K\quad(K\in\mathbb Z,\ K\ge2).}$$
The conclusion is the stated weighted, fixed-footprint unbounded gap. The unit example establishes the separate gap  $2>1$ .4.
